doc.title: Young Snooky — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Founding member of the Thad Jones-Mel Lewis band
summary: Young joined the Thad Jones-Mel Lewis band while on the Tonight Show, calls it the best band he played in, and remembers Thad as a close friend and roommate.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: So that was your gig and then you got, you were able to be a founding member of the Thad Jones-Mel Lewis. So here you were working with Thad in the NBC Band and then Thad forms another band with Mel Lewis, or forms a band with Mel Lewis and you were with that band.

That band you‘re talking about. Let‘s see who formed that band? I played in the first band when they first started because me and Thad was like that coming out of Basie‘s band. We were like brothers. So when he and Mel Lewis formed that band I was playing the Tonight Show and they asked me would I come play in that band. I said, ―Are you kidding? You know I‘m going to come, Thad!‖

You know, Thad and I was roommates and did everything together. So when he formed that band, that turned out to be quite a band, man. That band, I‘m sorry but, ain‘t no band I played that band, I‘ll tell you that!
And I‘ve played in quite a few bands since then.

And I ain‘t never played with no band, this band don‘t out play Thad and Mel Lewis‘s band, Mel Lewis playing drums and Thad playing the trumpet and flugelhorn and conducting out there. And Thad was something else, man. Great guy, man. Thad, I don‘t know, I don‘t know why we lost Thad, man. Thad wasn‘t that old or anything. He did few things that were probably against his health or something. Because he was a pretty strong guy, he was strong, you know? He wasn‘t no weak guy by no means, but I don‘t know, just like his brother still living, Hank.
Hank is still around. And his other brother played drums.
Elvin, I don‘t see, we lost Elvin, I don‘t see. Elvin was tough too man.
